controls.applicability: Applies to every organization developing, procuring, deploying, or permitting AI use.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every adopting organization requires an accountable governance mandate and decision rights.

controls.implementation_notes: Separate accountable ownership from advisory review and document conflicts or overlaps with existing risk functions.
controls.objective: Establish accountable authority for governing AI across the organization.
controls.requirement: The organization shall define and approve an AI governance mandate that assigns decision rights, accountable roles, escalation paths, oversight responsibilities, and authority to impose conditions, accept risk, suspend use, or require retirement.
controls.title: AI governance mandate and decision rights

controls.applicability: Applies whenever personnel or third parties may acquire, build, access, or use AI on the organization's behalf.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every governed AI use depends on organization-wide policy and acceptable-use boundaries.

controls.implementation_notes: Align with security, privacy, records, procurement, intellectual-property, and incident policies without duplicating them.
controls.objective: Communicate permitted, restricted, and prohibited AI activities.
controls.requirement: The organization shall maintain approved AI policies and supporting guidance that define authorized use, prohibited practices, user responsibilities, data boundaries, review triggers, exception handling, and consequences of noncompliance.
controls.title: AI policy and acceptable-use boundaries

controls.applicability: Applies to proposed, experimental, production, embedded, vendor-provided, and materially changed AI uses.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every proposed or operating AI system requires inventory coverage and accountable ownership.

controls.implementation_notes: Define scope rules for embedded features, user-acquired tools, experiments, models, agents, and retired systems.
controls.objective: Maintain visibility and accountability throughout the AI portfolio.
controls.requirement: The organization shall maintain a versioned inventory of AI systems and material AI use cases, with a stable identifier, named business owner, system owner, purpose, lifecycle state, deployment context, model or service dependencies, data categories, and current review status.
controls.title: AI inventory and accountable ownership

controls.applicability: Applies before approval, after material change, and when incidents or new information could alter the risk decision.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every AI system requires a context-appropriate risk and impact assessment.

controls.implementation_notes: Use qualitative judgment where precision is unsupported and route domain-specific issues to qualified reviewers.
controls.objective: Identify and evaluate material risks before use and when conditions change.
controls.requirement: Each AI system shall undergo a documented, context-appropriate assessment addressing intended and foreseeable use, affected parties, data, autonomy, external impact, security, privacy, safety, fairness, legal, operational, third-party, and reputational risks.
controls.title: AI risk and impact assessment

controls.applicability: Applies to roles that select, approve, build, configure, operate, monitor, review, or use AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every governed use depends on role-appropriate competence and awareness.

controls.implementation_notes: Measure practical understanding and refresh content following material changes or incidents.
controls.objective: Ensure people can fulfill AI governance, development, operation, and use responsibilities.
controls.requirement: The organization shall define required competencies and provide role-appropriate education for decision makers, reviewers, developers, operators, owners, procurement personnel, and users, including limitations, escalation, and responsible-use expectations.
controls.title: Competence and role-based awareness

controls.applicability: Applies to the enterprise governance system and should be scaled to portfolio size and risk.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The governance system requires independent challenge and continual improvement.

controls.implementation_notes: Independence may be organizational or procedural but reviewers must be able to challenge accountable owners.
controls.objective: Verify that AI governance remains suitable, implemented, and effective.
controls.requirement: The organization shall periodically review and independently challenge the design and operation of its AI governance system, track findings to accountable owners, and update controls in response to incidents, performance results, technology, obligations, and risk changes.
controls.title: Independent challenge and continual improvement

controls.applicability: Applies to developed, integrated, configured, or externally exposed AI systems; depth increases with access, autonomy, and impact.

applicability_metadata.rationale: External reach or elevated system access establishes a clear architecture and threat-modeling need.

controls.implementation_notes: Include prompts, retrieval, memory, tools, plugins, model endpoints, users, agents, and external content sources.
controls.objective: Identify trust boundaries, abuse paths, and failure modes before deployment.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall have documented architecture, data flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, privileged operations, and threat scenarios, with security requirements and mitigations incorporated into design and release decisions.
controls.title: Secure architecture and threat modeling

controls.applicability: Applies when an AI system accesses non-public data, services, tools, environments, or administrative functions.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Non-public information, system access, or tool capability establishes an identity and least-privilege need.

controls.implementation_notes: Distinguish user, application, service, model, and agent identities; avoid shared or embedded long-lived credentials.
controls.objective: Restrict AI access to authorized subjects and necessary resources.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall authenticate users and non-human actors, enforce authorization at each trust boundary, use least privilege and separation of duties, protect credentials, and periodically review access and privilege assignments.
controls.title: Identity, authentication, and least privilege

controls.applicability: Applies to generative AI receiving user input, retrieved content, files, messages, web content, tool output, or agent communications.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Tool use or external communication creates plausible untrusted-content pathways.

controls.implementation_notes: Detection alone is insufficient. Apply architectural isolation, least privilege, output validation, and action authorization.
controls.objective: Prevent untrusted content from overriding instructions or causing unauthorized behavior.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall treat user, retrieved, uploaded, and externally sourced content as untrusted; separate instructions from data; validate inputs and context; constrain downstream actions; and test direct, indirect, encoded, and multi-step manipulation paths.
controls.title: Untrusted input and prompt-injection defenses

controls.applicability: Applies when outputs reach users, code interpreters, browsers, databases, APIs, workflows, tools, or other AI systems.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every system output must be handled according to its receiving context and potential use.

controls.implementation_notes: Validate at the enforcement point and avoid relying on a model to approve its own output.
controls.objective: Prevent generated content from becoming an unsafe instruction, command, or disclosure.
controls.requirement: AI-generated output shall be treated as untrusted before display, execution, storage, transmission, or use by another component. The receiving context shall apply schema, encoding, content, authorization, and business-rule validation appropriate to the action.
controls.title: Safe output handling

controls.applicability: Applies to internally developed code and configurations and to material integration or customization of third-party AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The current intake does not identify whether code, configurations, integrations, or customizations are developed or maintained.

controls.implementation_notes: Include prompts, orchestration, retrieval pipelines, model configuration, infrastructure, and policy-as-code artifacts.
controls.objective: Reduce exploitable defects and unsafe changes across the AI system lifecycle.
controls.requirement: AI systems shall follow a secure development and change process that includes code and configuration review, dependency analysis, secrets protection, security testing, vulnerability remediation, environment separation, release approval, and equivalent security, quality, and license checks for code or configuration artifacts created or modified by agents.
controls.title: Secure development, testing, and vulnerability management

controls.applicability: Applies to production, externally accessible, usage-priced, agentic, recursive, or computationally intensive AI systems.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Autonomy, tools, external reach, or consequential action creates resource and service-abuse exposure.

controls.implementation_notes: Apply limits per user, identity, agent, tool, tenant, and workflow where aggregate limits could mask abuse.
controls.objective: Limit denial of service, runaway consumption, and financially harmful use.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall enforce resource, rate, concurrency, recursion, token, time, and financial limits appropriate to its operating context and shall fail safely when limits or dependency thresholds are reached.
controls.title: Resource and service abuse protection

controls.applicability: Applies whenever an AI system processes or generates data, including prompts, outputs, embeddings, logs, feedback, and memory.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every AI system processes or generates data and requires authorized use and minimization.

controls.implementation_notes: Reassess secondary use, model improvement, telemetry, and provider use separately from the primary business purpose.
controls.objective: Limit AI processing to necessary, lawful, and approved information.
controls.requirement: Data used to develop, configure, test, retrieve for, operate, monitor, or improve an AI system shall have a documented authorized purpose and shall be limited to the minimum categories, fields, volume, precision, and retention needed for that purpose.
controls.title: Authorized data use and minimization

controls.applicability: Applies to non-public, personal, regulated, confidential, security-sensitive, or contractually restricted information.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Non-public information requires protection proportionate to its sensitivity.

controls.implementation_notes: Include derived data and embeddings where they can reveal or reconstruct sensitive source information.
controls.objective: Apply protection proportionate to data sensitivity throughout AI processing.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall classify information and enforce approved access, encryption, transmission, storage, isolation, masking, loss-prevention, and disposal safeguards across prompts, outputs, retrieval stores, training data, logs, caches, and memory.
controls.title: Data classification and protection

controls.applicability: Applies to training, fine-tuning, evaluation, retrieval, grounding, feedback, and decision-support data.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The current intake does not describe training, retrieval, grounding, evaluation, or decision-support data sources.

controls.implementation_notes: Record known gaps and avoid implying that provenance alone establishes accuracy, fairness, or legal permissibility.
controls.objective: Support reliable, traceable, and authorized use of data and knowledge sources.
controls.requirement: Material data and knowledge sources shall be documented with origin, ownership or license basis, transformations, quality limitations, update method, and permitted uses, and shall be evaluated for representativeness, integrity, poisoning, and contamination risks.
controls.title: Data provenance, quality, and permitted sourcing

controls.applicability: Applies when personal data is used or when outputs can identify, profile, infer about, or materially affect individuals.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Consequential decision impact establishes a plausible need for individual protections and privacy review.

controls.implementation_notes: Include inferred attributes, model memory, embeddings, monitoring data, and provider-retained interactions.
controls.objective: Identify and manage privacy effects on individuals throughout the AI lifecycle.
controls.requirement: AI processing involving personal data shall undergo appropriate privacy review and implement required notice, choice, rights handling, access restrictions, minimization, retention, correction, deletion, and protections against inappropriate inference or re-identification.
controls.title: Privacy assessment and individual protections

controls.applicability: Applies from concept or procurement and must remain current through retirement.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every AI system requires documented purpose, boundaries, limitations, and success criteria.

controls.implementation_notes: Avoid broad purpose statements that permit uncontrolled expansion; identify foreseeable misuse and out-of-scope contexts.
controls.objective: Establish clear boundaries against which the AI system can be evaluated and governed.
controls.requirement: Each AI system shall document its intended purpose, users, affected parties, operating context, permitted and prohibited uses, dependencies, assumptions, known limitations, human responsibilities, and measurable acceptance and failure criteria.
controls.title: Intended use, limitations, and success criteria

controls.applicability: Applies before initial production use and material releases; test depth follows context and potential impact.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every AI system requires proportionate evaluation and release-readiness criteria before use.

controls.implementation_notes: Separate model benchmarks from end-to-end system validation and document test representativeness and uncertainty.
controls.objective: Demonstrate that the AI system performs acceptably and fails within understood boundaries.
controls.requirement: Before release, each exact AI system version shall be evaluated in its intended configuration and operating context using representative and adversarial scenarios against approved criteria for task performance, security, privacy, safety, reliability, harmful content, bias or impact, human oversight, and recovery as relevant. Material outcomes shall also be subject to defined post-action validation, with pre-finalization checks for high-impact or difficult-to-reverse actions.
controls.title: Evaluation, validation, and release readiness

controls.applicability: Applies to planned changes, provider-driven changes, emergency changes, and discovered drift in system behavior or context.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every AI system requires defined material-change and reassessment triggers.

controls.implementation_notes: New tool access, write authority, persistent memory, or external reach should be treated as material by default.
controls.objective: Prevent changes from bypassing established risk decisions and controls.
controls.requirement: The organization shall define material-change criteria and reassess affected AI systems before or promptly after changes to purpose, model, data, prompts, retrieval, tools, permissions, autonomy, users, reach, vendor terms, environment, or applicable obligations.
controls.title: Material change and reassessment

controls.applicability: Applies to production, externally used, vendor-dependent, or data-bearing AI systems.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Non-public data, external reach, or operational impact establishes a clear suspension and retirement need.

controls.implementation_notes: Address downstream consumers, cached outputs, embedded models, integrations, contract termination, and legal holds.
controls.objective: End AI use safely and remove residual access, data, and dependency exposure.
controls.requirement: Each production AI system shall have criteria and procedures for suspension and retirement, including user and stakeholder communication, access revocation, data and credential disposition, dependency handling, record preservation, and verification of completion.
controls.title: Suspension and retirement

controls.applicability: Applies when AI can plan, invoke tools, access services, communicate with agents, or execute actions beyond content generation.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Autonomous operation, tools, communication, delegation, memory, or action authority establishes agent identity and authority needs.

controls.implementation_notes: Preserve the chain from human or service principal to agent and downstream action; prohibit privilege laundering. Prefer short-lived, resource-scoped credentials or action permits kept outside model context and bind them to the authorized holder where the platform supports it.
controls.objective: Make each agent accountable and restrict its authority to an approved purpose.
controls.requirement: Each agent shall use an attributable non-human identity and operate under explicitly delegated authority that binds approved purpose, task, target resources, data, tools, actions, environments, limits, validity period, and escalation conditions, with privileges no broader than the initiating principal and approved service role require.
controls.title: Agent identity and delegated authority

controls.applicability: Applies to every agent with tool, connector, plugin, code-execution, messaging, workflow, or system access.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Tool capability, system access, or modification authority requires explicit connector and action boundaries.

controls.implementation_notes: Expose narrow task-specific functions instead of general shells, broad APIs, or unrestricted browsers where practical.
controls.objective: Prevent agents from using capabilities or parameters outside approved scope.
controls.requirement: Agent tools, connectors, APIs, destinations, operations, parameters, runtime resources, and credential delivery shall be governed through bounded, versioned capability profiles and enforced outside the model, with least privilege, schema validation, transaction and rate limits, isolated execution where appropriate, environment separation, and denial by default when required context cannot be verified.
controls.title: Tool, connector, and action boundaries

controls.applicability: Applies when agents can modify records, send communications, execute code, make commitments, move value, affect rights, or change production systems.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Material actions or external communication require approval boundaries and irreversible-action safeguards.

controls.implementation_notes: Avoid approval fatigue, bundled approvals, self-approval, and prompts that conceal the actual tool parameters or destination.
controls.objective: Preserve meaningful human control over consequential or difficult-to-reverse actions.
controls.requirement: Agents shall require an authenticated, informed decision independent of the requesting agent before defined high-impact, externally binding, privileged, destructive, financial, safety-relevant, or difficult-to-reverse actions. The decision interface shall present the proposed action, basis, scope, and consequences and shall support step-up verification or temporary, automatically expiring authority when current session or delegation assurance is insufficient.
controls.title: Human approval and irreversible-action safeguards

controls.applicability: Applies to agents that retain conversation, task, user, organizational, vector, episodic, or cross-session state.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Persistent memory directly establishes a need to protect agent state.

controls.implementation_notes: Separate instructions, observations, user data, and learned preferences and prevent cross-user or cross-tenant leakage.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorized disclosure, poisoning, persistence, or cross-context influence through agent memory.
controls.requirement: Persistent and working memory shall be authorized, scoped, isolated, integrity-protected, access-controlled, monitored, and subject to correction, retention, and deletion controls; untrusted content shall not become durable instruction or trusted state without validation.
controls.title: Agent memory and state protection

controls.applicability: Applies when agents communicate, delegate, coordinate, negotiate, or invoke other autonomous or semi-autonomous agents.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Delegation capability establishes multi-agent trust and control requirements.

controls.implementation_notes: Treat agent output as untrusted input and design for compromised, unavailable, misaligned, or looping participants.
controls.objective: Bound authority propagation and cascading behavior across interacting agents.
controls.requirement: Multi-agent systems shall authenticate participants, validate messages, restrict which agents may delegate or receive tasks, prevent authority expansion, preserve originating context, record each delegation hop, limit recursion and propagation, and preserve traceability across task handoffs and resulting actions.
controls.title: Multi-agent and delegation controls

controls.applicability: Applies to agents with production access, material reach, autonomous action, privileged tools, or difficult-to-reverse effects.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Autonomy, privilege, broad reach, material action, or difficult reversibility requires containment and emergency-stop design.

controls.implementation_notes: Test whether in-flight tasks, delegated agents, queued actions, and cached credentials actually stop.
controls.objective: Limit harmful activity and restore control when agent behavior deviates from approved boundaries.
controls.requirement: Agentic systems shall provide independently enforceable containment, credential and delegated grant revocation, action interruption, version and component quarantine, rollback, and emergency-disable mechanisms that operators can invoke without relying on the affected model or agent.
controls.title: Agent containment and emergency stop

controls.applicability: Applies to production systems; scope increases for consequential, external, privileged, or agentic use.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The current intake does not establish lifecycle stage or operational deployment.

controls.implementation_notes: Do not indiscriminately log sensitive prompts or outputs; use structured metadata, redaction, and tiered access where appropriate.
controls.objective: Reconstruct material AI decisions, interactions, and actions without excessive collection.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall generate protected, time-synchronized, completeness-checked records with stable run or trace identifiers sufficient to correlate initiating principal, agent, deployment, runtime composition, task, inputs, outputs, model and configuration versions, retrieval sources, delegated authority, tool calls, targets, approvals, requested and executed actions, policy decisions, results, outcomes, cost, and errors, subject to minimization and retention controls.
controls.title: Logging and traceability

controls.applicability: Applies to production systems; near-real-time monitoring is expected where delayed detection could materially increase harm.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The current intake does not establish production monitoring scope, frequency, or detection needs.

controls.implementation_notes: Combine model, application, user, agent, infrastructure, and business-process signals rather than relying on one metric.
controls.objective: Detect drift, misuse, failures, and operation outside approved boundaries.
controls.requirement: Production AI systems shall be monitored using defined indicators, thresholds, and review responsibilities for performance, harmful or anomalous behavior, access, tool use, destinations, resource consumption, policy violations, data exposure, control failure, dependency health, changing risk conditions, and actions that are permitted but materially inconsistent with approved purpose or task.
controls.title: Behavioral and control monitoring

controls.applicability: Applies to the enterprise and all operational AI systems, including relevant vendor incidents and near misses.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every operational AI system depends on enterprise incident response and reporting capability.

controls.implementation_notes: Cover harmful output, data disclosure, prompt or memory compromise, unauthorized action, model failure, abuse, and provider outage.
controls.objective: Contain, investigate, communicate, and learn from AI-related incidents.
controls.requirement: The organization shall integrate AI failure and misuse scenarios into incident management, with defined reporting channels, severity criteria, roles, evidence preservation, containment, stakeholder notification, recovery, root-cause analysis, and control improvement.
controls.title: AI incident response and reporting

controls.applicability: Applies when AI supports material operations, external services, automated action, or processes with availability or integrity requirements.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Operational impact, external reach, material action, or difficult reversibility establishes resilience and recovery needs.

controls.implementation_notes: A fallback model may share the same failure mode; validate independence and the safety of non-AI alternatives.
controls.objective: Maintain acceptable outcomes when models, data, tools, providers, or controls fail.
controls.requirement: The AI system shall define and test safe-failure behavior, dependency timeouts, approved non-agent or manual fallback procedures where continuity requires them, backup and restoration where relevant, rollback, reconciliation, recovery objectives, and criteria for degraded operation or suspension.
controls.title: Resilience, safe failure, and recovery

controls.applicability: Applies to hosted models, AI applications, platforms, embedded AI features, data services, agents, plugins, and material support providers.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The current intake does not establish whether an external AI supplier or service is used.

controls.implementation_notes: Tailor depth to dependency and impact and record unanswered questions, compensating controls, and acceptance authority.
controls.objective: Understand and manage risk introduced by external AI providers and services.
controls.requirement: Before use and periodically thereafter, the organization shall evaluate relevant AI suppliers for security, privacy, resilience, governance, data use, model practices, isolation, incident response, subprocessors, legal terms, assurance, financial viability, and service dependency.
controls.title: AI supplier and service due diligence

controls.applicability: Applies where third-party AI processes organizational data, supports material operations, or creates meaningful legal, security, privacy, or dependency exposure.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Supplier involvement and contractual exposure are not represented in the canonical assessment.

controls.implementation_notes: Verify that product configuration and actual service behavior match negotiated terms; click-through terms may change independently.
controls.objective: Make material supplier responsibilities enforceable and transparent.
controls.requirement: Agreements for material AI services shall address permitted data use, model training or improvement, confidentiality, security, privacy, retention and deletion, isolation, subprocessors, incident notification, service changes, assurance rights, continuity, intellectual property, termination assistance, and allocation of responsibilities.
controls.title: Contractual AI safeguards

controls.applicability: Applies to externally sourced, open-source, pretrained, downloaded, imported, or dynamically loaded components.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Component sourcing, provenance, and loading behavior are not represented in the canonical assessment.

controls.implementation_notes: Maintain an AI bill of materials appropriate to the system and address mutable tags, remote code, unsafe serialization, and abandoned packages.
controls.objective: Reduce compromise, tampering, and unknown risk in AI components and dependencies.
controls.requirement: Models, datasets, libraries, containers, plugins, extensions, prompts, agent instructions, tool definitions, requested permissions, and other material components shall come from approved sources, have documented and runtime-resolved versions and provenance, be integrity-checked where feasible, and undergo security, license, and risk review before use or update. Unapproved or integrity-breaking changes shall be blocked or quarantined.
controls.title: Component provenance and integrity

controls.applicability: Applies to material third-party AI services and components throughout the relationship.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Material supplier and subprocessor relationships are not represented in the canonical assessment.

controls.implementation_notes: Define notification expectations and technical detection where providers do not offer reliable version or change transparency.
controls.objective: Prevent unreviewed supplier changes from altering approved risk conditions.
controls.requirement: Material supplier and subprocessor changes shall be identified, assessed, and governed, including changes to models, training or data use, hosting location, security controls, features, terms, subprocessors, service levels, ownership, and end-of-life status.
controls.title: Supplier change and subprocessor oversight

controls.applicability: Applies where loss or material change of a provider, model, platform, or data source could disrupt important operations or control effectiveness.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Provider concentration, continuity, and exit dependencies require information not present in the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Consider proprietary prompts, evaluation assets, embeddings, fine-tunes, logs, integrations, and skills required to migrate.
controls.objective: Limit operational and strategic harm from supplier failure, lock-in, or withdrawal.
controls.requirement: Material AI dependencies shall be assessed for concentration, portability, service failure, provider discontinuation, acquisition, and lock-in risk, with tested continuity, migration, data return or deletion, and orderly exit arrangements where warranted.
controls.title: Concentration, continuity, and exit planning

controls.applicability: Applies to the enterprise AI governance program and material AI initiatives.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every governed AI portfolio depends on defined responsible-AI objectives and measures.

controls.implementation_notes: Objectives should be measurable where practicable and should not imply unsupported precision or universal fairness.
controls.objective: Translate responsible AI principles into governed and measurable outcomes.
controls.requirement: The organization shall define, approve, measure, and periodically review objectives for responsible AI development and use, including relevant fairness, transparency, reliability, safety, security, privacy, and oversight outcomes.
controls.title: Responsible AI objectives and measures

controls.applicability: Applies whenever an applicable AI requirement cannot be met as designed.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Exception and residual-risk treatment depends on whether an applicable requirement cannot be met as designed.

controls.implementation_notes: Do not use exceptions to bypass prohibited uses or non-waivable legal obligations.
controls.objective: Ensure deviations are visible, authorized, temporary, and risk informed.
controls.requirement: Exceptions to AI controls shall document scope, rationale, affected systems, residual risk, compensating measures, accountable approval, expiration, and review or closure criteria.
controls.title: AI exceptions and residual-risk acceptance

controls.applicability: Applies to the enterprise AI governance system.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every governed AI portfolio depends on periodic management review of the governance system.

controls.implementation_notes: Use a cadence proportionate to portfolio change and risk rather than relying only on an annual review.
controls.objective: Maintain leadership visibility and direction over AI governance performance.
controls.requirement: Leadership shall periodically review AI portfolio risk, performance, incidents, complaints, exceptions, assurance results, resource adequacy, changes in obligations, and improvement actions, and shall record decisions and accountable actions.
controls.title: AI governance management review

controls.applicability: Applies enterprise-wide and to systems affecting external parties.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every AI system requires a route for concerns, misuse, and adverse impacts to be reported and escalated.

controls.implementation_notes: Coordinate with whistleblowing, complaints, privacy, product support, and incident processes while protecting reporters.
controls.objective: Enable timely reporting and investigation of suspected AI harm or misconduct.
controls.requirement: The organization shall provide accessible and protected channels for personnel and relevant external parties to report AI concerns, adverse impacts, misuse, or control failures and shall triage, investigate, remediate, and track reports.
controls.title: AI concerns and adverse-impact reporting

controls.applicability: Applies to workforce and third-party use of AI on the organization's behalf.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every assessed use depends on an enterprise process for approving AI tools and configurations.

controls.implementation_notes: Include embedded AI features and user-enabled connectors, not only standalone AI products.
controls.objective: Prevent unmanaged enterprise use of AI services and features.
controls.requirement: The organization shall define approved AI tools, models, features, plugins, connectors, and configuration baselines and shall identify, restrict, or remediate unauthorized use.
controls.title: Approved AI tools and configurations

controls.applicability: Applies to AI users, owners, approvers, developers, operators, and reviewers.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every assessed use depends on role-appropriate AI literacy and awareness.

controls.implementation_notes: Distinguish general literacy from specialist engineering, legal, validation, and oversight competence.
controls.objective: Equip users to recognize AI capabilities, limitations, obligations, and escalation needs.
controls.requirement: Personnel using or overseeing AI shall receive role-appropriate literacy and awareness covering permitted use, data handling, output verification, human responsibility, known limitations, misuse, and concern reporting.
controls.title: AI literacy and user awareness

controls.applicability: Applies when incorrect output could create more than negligible harm.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Operational or consequential impact establishes a clear need for user verification of material outputs.

controls.implementation_notes: Define what verification means for the context and avoid meaningless human approval that lacks time, information, or authority.
controls.objective: Reduce harm from overreliance on incorrect or unsuitable AI output.
controls.requirement: Material AI outputs shall be verified against authoritative sources or qualified judgment before consequential decisions, external communication, code deployment, or legal, regulatory, financial, safety, or security use.
controls.title: User verification of material AI outputs

controls.applicability: Applies whenever personnel can submit organizational or third-party information to AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Workforce AI use depends on enterprise rules for confidential and restricted information.

controls.implementation_notes: Address prompts, uploads, connectors, meeting content, code, outputs, feedback, and provider retention.
controls.objective: Prevent personnel from exposing protected information through AI tools.
controls.requirement: The organization shall specify which information classifications may be entered into each approved AI service and enforce restrictions through guidance, configuration, access control, and monitoring appropriate to risk.
controls.title: Confidential and restricted information use boundaries

controls.applicability: Applies across technology, procurement, cloud, SaaS, development, and workforce environments.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Reliable governance depends on enterprise discovery and reconciliation beyond self-reported intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Define tolerances and ownership for shadow AI rather than assuming questionnaires provide complete coverage.
controls.objective: Identify unregistered and materially incomplete AI use.
controls.requirement: The organization shall use proportionate discovery methods to identify AI services, embedded features, models, endpoints, agents, components, connectors, and material use cases across source, cloud, endpoint, identity, SaaS, gateway, network, and runtime evidence and reconcile findings to the approved inventory.
controls.title: AI discovery and inventory reconciliation

controls.applicability: Applies throughout the lifecycle of material AI systems and agents.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every material AI system requires documented models, services, data sources, tools, and dependencies.

controls.implementation_notes: Link records to versions and owners so changes can trigger targeted reassessment.
controls.objective: Record the resources required to develop, operate, oversee, change, and retire AI.
controls.requirement: Each material AI system shall document its data, models, prompts, tools, integrations, compute, environments, identities and effective access, human competencies, suppliers, downstream agents, and operational dependencies, including approved and observed runtime composition where agentic components can resolve dynamically.
controls.title: AI resource and dependency documentation

controls.applicability: Applies to proposed, experimental, approved, production, suspended, and retired AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every inventory record requires a current lifecycle state and proportionate review.

controls.implementation_notes: Expired experiments and ownerless systems should not remain implicitly authorized.
controls.objective: Keep inventory decisions aligned with actual system status and business need.
controls.requirement: AI systems shall have controlled lifecycle states, review dates, approval and exception status, accountable exception owners and expiry dates, retained decision history, and criteria for experimentation, production, suspension, decommissioning, and archival.
controls.title: AI lifecycle status and review

controls.applicability: Applies where AI may be subject to legal, regulatory, contractual, or sector requirements.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Legal, regulatory, contractual, and sector applicability is not established by the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Classification is context dependent and should be validated by qualified counsel where material.
controls.objective: Determine which legal and regulatory duties apply to an AI use.
controls.requirement: The organization shall document relevant jurisdictions, organizational roles, system classifications, prohibited or restricted practices, transparency duties, and sector-specific obligations before approval and after material change.
controls.title: AI regulatory role and applicability classification

controls.applicability: Applies to consequential, externally facing, employee-facing, or otherwise materially impactful AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Consequential impact or external reach establishes a need for a proportionate AI impact assessment.

controls.implementation_notes: Keep impact assessment distinct from technical security risk assessment while coordinating shared facts and treatments.
controls.objective: Identify potential effects on individuals, groups, customers, workers, and society.
controls.requirement: Material AI systems shall undergo a documented impact assessment addressing intended and foreseeable effects, affected parties, severity, likelihood, distribution of benefits and harms, accessibility, contestability, and mitigation.
controls.title: AI impact assessment

controls.applicability: Applies to risks identified through intake, assessment, testing, monitoring, incidents, or assurance.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every completed assessment requires documented treatment of identified risks and accountable acceptance of remaining risk.

controls.implementation_notes: Track dependencies and aggregate portfolio risk rather than closing issues solely because an owner accepted them.
controls.objective: Ensure identified AI risks lead to accountable decisions and verified treatment.
controls.requirement: Identified AI risks shall have documented treatment decisions, owners, deadlines, control dependencies, acceptance authority, and verification of completion and residual risk.
controls.title: AI risk treatment and residual-risk approval

controls.applicability: Applies to purchased, licensed, collected, scraped, generated, customer-provided, open, and third-party data.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Data acquisition methods and usage rights are not represented in the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Public availability does not by itself establish permission, suitability, accuracy, or absence of personal data.
controls.objective: Ensure data is obtained and used under documented authority and restrictions.
controls.requirement: Data acquired for AI development, evaluation, retrieval, operation, or improvement shall have documented source, ownership or license basis, permitted uses, restrictions, retention, and required approvals.
controls.title: AI data acquisition and rights

controls.applicability: Applies to training, fine-tuning, evaluation, retrieval, grounding, and feedback data.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Training, evaluation, retrieval, grounding, and feedback transformations are not represented in the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Preserve enough lineage to reproduce material datasets and investigate errors without retaining unnecessary personal data.
controls.objective: Make data-selection and preparation decisions repeatable and reviewable.
controls.requirement: The organization shall define and record criteria and methods for selecting, cleaning, labeling, filtering, transforming, augmenting, excluding, and versioning data used by AI systems.
controls.title: AI data preparation and transformation

controls.applicability: Applies where data materially affects model behavior, retrieval, evaluation, or decisions.

applicability_metadata.rationale: The current intake does not establish whether data quality or representativeness materially affects behavior or decisions.

controls.implementation_notes: Quality is purpose-specific; document gaps rather than asserting that a dataset is universally representative.
controls.objective: Ensure data is suitable for the intended AI purpose and affected population.
controls.requirement: Data used by material AI systems shall be evaluated against defined requirements for relevance, accuracy, completeness, timeliness, integrity, representativeness, bias, and known limitations.
controls.title: AI data quality and representativeness

controls.applicability: Applies to retrieval-augmented generation, enterprise search, knowledge assistants, and agent memory retrieval.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Retrieval, grounding, enterprise search, and memory-retrieval behavior are not represented in the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Validate authorization at retrieval time and account for stale indexes, copied chunks, embeddings, caches, and derived stores.
controls.objective: Keep retrieved knowledge authorized, current, traceable, and correctly access filtered.
controls.requirement: Retrieval systems shall govern source approval, provenance, update cadence, integrity, user-level authorization, tenant isolation, relevance, citation, and removal from source through index.
controls.title: Retrieval and grounding governance

controls.applicability: Applies to systems or providers with feedback loops, adaptive behavior, or improvement features.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Feedback loops, adaptive behavior, and provider product-improvement settings are not represented in the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Treat product-improvement telemetry as a distinct purpose requiring an explicit decision.
controls.objective: Prevent unreviewed operational data from changing AI behavior or training use.
controls.requirement: Prompts, outputs, user feedback, monitoring data, and operational interactions shall not be used for model training, tuning, reinforcement, or evaluation unless the use is authorized, minimized, quality controlled, and isolated from untrusted manipulation.
controls.title: Feedback and learning-data governance

controls.applicability: Applies to internally or externally supplied models used in material AI systems.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every material AI system requires model and behavior-configuration traceability.

controls.implementation_notes: Record provider-managed model aliases and detect silent version changes where feasible.
controls.objective: Maintain traceability of approved models and behavior-affecting configuration.
controls.requirement: The organization shall inventory approved models, versions, adapters, fine-tunes, system prompts, safety settings, endpoints, and deployment locations and shall preserve version and approval history.
controls.title: Model inventory and version control

controls.applicability: Applies to new models and material model substitutions.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every material model requires documented suitability evaluation and approval for its intended use.

controls.implementation_notes: A more capable model may introduce unnecessary autonomy, data exposure, cost, or concentration risk.
controls.objective: Select models that are suitable, lawful, supportable, and proportionate to the use.
controls.requirement: Models shall be evaluated and approved for intended capability, limitations, data handling, licensing, security, safety, performance, support, location, and dependency risk before material use.
controls.title: Model selection and approval

controls.applicability: Applies to material production AI and controlled preproduction environments.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Production status and the scope of model, prompt, retrieval, and safety-setting changes are not established by the intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Define materiality triggers for provider-managed updates and emergency changes.
controls.objective: Prevent untested changes from invalidating an approved AI risk decision.
controls.requirement: Changes to models, versions, adapters, fine-tuning, prompts, parameters, guardrails, tools, retrieval sources, and safety settings shall be versioned, impact assessed, tested, approved, monitored, and reversible where feasible.
controls.title: Model and behavior-configuration change control

controls.applicability: Applies to models whose behavior materially affects system outcomes.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Operational or consequential outcomes establish a clear need for model evaluation and acceptance thresholds.

controls.implementation_notes: Separate model evaluation from end-to-end system validation and record uncertainty and known test limitations.
controls.objective: Demonstrate that a selected or changed model meets defined use-case requirements.
controls.requirement: Material models shall be evaluated using representative and adversarial tests against documented performance, robustness, security, safety, fairness, and reliability thresholds before approval and after relevant change.
controls.title: Model evaluation and acceptance thresholds

controls.applicability: Applies to shared, hosted, multi-tenant, or multi-environment AI platforms.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Shared, hosted, multi-tenant, and multi-environment platform architecture is not represented in the intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Test both management-plane and data-plane boundaries, including embeddings and derived artifacts.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorized access or data movement across platform trust boundaries.
controls.requirement: AI platforms shall isolate tenants, environments, workloads, model endpoints, retrieval stores, caches, logs, and memory according to approved identity and data-classification boundaries.
controls.title: AI platform and tenant isolation

controls.applicability: Applies to platform administration, model deployment, safety settings, data stores, gateways, and tenant configuration.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Privileged system access establishes an AI platform administration control need.

controls.implementation_notes: Include vendor support access and break-glass accounts in the control design.
controls.objective: Protect high-impact AI platform and model-management functions.
controls.requirement: Privileged AI platform access shall use named identities, strong authentication, least privilege, separation of duties, time-bound elevation where feasible, logging, and periodic access review.
controls.title: AI platform privileged administration

controls.applicability: Applies to internal and external model endpoints, gateways, brokers, and AI service APIs.

applicability_metadata.rationale: External reach, protected service access, or tool use establishes an endpoint and gateway governance need.

controls.implementation_notes: Enforce authorization outside the model and distinguish user, application, agent, and service identities.
controls.objective: Apply consistent policy enforcement to model and AI-service interfaces.
controls.requirement: Model endpoints and AI APIs shall be inventoried, authenticated, authorized, scoped, rate limited, monitored, and protected against unauthorized models, data flows, tools, and destinations.
controls.title: AI endpoint and gateway governance

controls.applicability: Applies to consequential, externally impactful, automated, safety-relevant, or high-autonomy AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Autonomy, consequential impact, external reach, or material action establishes a need for effective human oversight.

controls.implementation_notes: Human presence alone is insufficient if the reviewer lacks information, time, authority, or a practical intervention mechanism.
controls.objective: Give qualified people effective authority to understand, challenge, override, or stop AI operation.
controls.requirement: Material AI systems shall define oversight roles, required competence, information and interfaces, intervention points, escalation paths, override authority, and conditions for suspension or safe continuation.
controls.title: Human oversight design and authority

controls.applicability: Applies to consequential decision support and automated decision processes.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Consequential decision impact establishes accountability and contestability requirements.

controls.implementation_notes: Avoid treating an AI recommendation as neutral evidence or transferring accountability to a vendor or model.
controls.objective: Preserve accountable decision ownership and appropriate routes to challenge AI-influenced outcomes.
controls.requirement: The organization shall assign accountability for AI-influenced decisions and provide proportionate review, appeal, correction, or contest mechanisms when outcomes can materially affect individuals or customers.
controls.title: Human decision accountability and contestability

controls.applicability: Applies to user-facing, customer-facing, synthetic-content, and materially decision-influencing AI.

applicability_metadata.rationale: External reach or material decision influence establishes a clear disclosure and user-information need.

controls.implementation_notes: Disclosure should be understandable and useful, not merely a generic disclaimer.
controls.objective: Provide users and affected parties with information needed for safe and informed interaction.
controls.requirement: AI systems shall provide context-appropriate disclosure of AI interaction or generated content and communicate intended use, limitations, human responsibilities, support, and material risks where required or appropriate.
controls.title: AI disclosure and user information

controls.applicability: Applies where changing data, models, providers, or context can materially affect outcomes.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Production status and material model, data, retrieval, provider, and context drift are not established by the intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Use outcome and control indicators, not only statistical drift, and account for low-volume consequential use.
controls.objective: Detect changes that could invalidate performance, safety, or control assumptions.
controls.requirement: Production AI shall monitor relevant changes in model behavior, input and reference data, embeddings, retrieval quality, performance, and control effectiveness against defined thresholds and trigger investigation or reassessment.
controls.title: Model, data, and retrieval drift monitoring

controls.applicability: Applies to findings from monitoring, incidents, complaints, testing, audit, and management review.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Every governed AI system depends on a process to record, correct, and verify material deficiencies and nonconformities.

controls.implementation_notes: Closure should require evidence of effectiveness rather than completion of an administrative task.
controls.objective: Correct control failures and prevent recurrence.
controls.requirement: AI nonconformities and material deficiencies shall be recorded, contained, root-caused, remediated, verified for effectiveness, and used to update relevant controls, assessments, tests, and guidance.
controls.title: AI nonconformity and corrective action

controls.applicability: Applies when third-party AI receives organizational, customer, employee, or other non-public data.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Third-party involvement and provider training or improvement settings are not established by the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Address prompts, outputs, uploads, feedback, telemetry, embeddings, and derived datasets separately.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorized vendor use of organizational data to train or improve AI.
controls.requirement: Contracts and service configurations shall prohibit provider training, fine-tuning, evaluation, or product improvement using organizational data unless the use is explicitly authorized, bounded, documented, and monitored.
controls.title: Vendor customer-data training restrictions

controls.applicability: Applies where suppliers store or derive artifacts from organizational data.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Supplier storage and derivation of AI artifacts are not established by the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Define treatment of backups, legal holds, de-identified data, and artifacts embedded in trained or tuned models.
controls.objective: Ensure organizational data and AI-derived artifacts can be securely removed or returned.
controls.requirement: Material AI suppliers shall support verified deletion or return of customer data, prompts, outputs, embeddings, fine-tunes, memory, logs, and derived artifacts upon request, expiration, or termination, subject to documented legal exceptions.
controls.title: Vendor AI artifact deletion and return

controls.applicability: Applies to material third-party AI services and dependencies.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Material third-party services and their incident obligations are not established by the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: Align supplier obligations with the organization's regulatory, customer, and operational reporting timelines.
controls.objective: Obtain timely information and assistance for AI-related incidents and failures.
controls.requirement: Supplier agreements shall define AI security, privacy, misuse, availability, model-behavior, and control incidents; notification timelines; required information; evidence preservation; cooperation; remediation; and continuing updates.
controls.title: Vendor AI incident notification and cooperation

controls.applicability: Applies where supplier failure could create material security, privacy, compliance, resilience, or customer impact.

applicability_metadata.rationale: Supplier materiality and available assurance are not established by the current intake.

controls.implementation_notes: General security reports may not cover model behavior, training-data use, tenant isolation, or AI-specific incident processes.
controls.objective: Obtain sufficient evidence that material supplier AI controls operate as represented.
controls.requirement: The organization shall obtain proportionate independent assurance, testing information, control evidence, and contractual assessment or audit rights for material AI suppliers and shall track deficiencies and limitations.
controls.title: Vendor AI assurance and audit rights

library.description: An independently authored enterprise AI control library covering organizational AI governance, workforce use, AI systems, models, platforms, agents, data, operations, and third parties. Each control includes structured, machine-readable applicability metadata. The metadata expresses control authority; consuming decision services evaluate submitted facts. Controls do not require an external-framework mapping to be valid.
limitations: Does not establish legal compliance, certification, or standards conformity.
Requires organization-specific tailoring, ownership, testing, and approval.
Does not contain a risk-tier selection or recommendation engine.
library.name: Independent AI Control Library
